title: Seal a loaded container door: thread an ISO 17712 bolt seal through the cam keeper hasp and close its barrel
instruction: A loaded shipping container's right door stands across the far side of the table, its face toward the robot (blue). Two steel hasps stick out of it, each a pair of upright ears with one round 16 mm seal hole through both, the holes running left to right. One is the cam keeper at the bottom of the door's centre-most locking bar (the grey bar rises from it); the other is the door handle's retainer (a yellow handle tab sits between its ears). A red ISO 17712 bolt seal lies on the table in two parts: the bolt (a headed pin) in a black tray on the left, and the barrel (the locking body, open end toward the left) on the right. Seal the door as the CTPAT seal procedure says: on the cam keeper, not on the door handle. The bolt goes through both ears and the barrel closes on its tip from the other side, seated against the bolt's shoulder. A seal closes for good: a barrel seated on a bolt not through the keeper is spent. Then let go and move both grippers at least 10 mm from the seal.
context: CBP CTPAT Job Aid, Seal Security Procedures (October 19, 2021): seals "must meet or exceed the most currently ISO 17712 standards for high security seals (qualifying cable or bolt seals are acceptable)", and "The high security seal used must be placed on the Secure Cam position, if available, instead of the right door handle. The seal must be placed at the bottom of the center most vertical bar of the right container door." Seal sizes from the J. J. Keller HBSCP8 coated pin bolt seal spec sheet (pin 87.0 x 22.2 mm, pin 8.0 mm steel and 11.8 mm coated, barrel 31.6 x 21.6 mm, assembled 95.9 mm), sold for trailer and intermodal container door latches. Done by: heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (2.2 million jobs in 2025, BLS) and dock workers who seal each loaded trailer or container.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table. Fixed, no joints: a blue door panel (4 mm, 0.6 m wide, 0.2 m tall) at x 0.41 with two steel hasps toward the robot. Each hasp is two 5 mm ears with an 8 mm gap between them (18 mm stack), 85 mm deep (x 0.325-0.41), 44 mm tall, with a 12-sided 16 mm seal hole (face to face) through both on an axis along y at x 0.345. Cam keeper (correct): hole at y 0.02, 60 mm over the table, a grey 22 mm locking bar stub rising above it to 125 mm over the table. Handle retainer (wrong): hole at y -0.20, 100 mm over the table, a yellow tab between its ears above the hole. Loose, two rigid bodies, red: the bolt (40 g): head 22.2 mm across, 6.4 mm long; pin 80.6 mm below it, 11.8 mm coated for 57.9 mm, a 45 deg taper (shoulder), then an 8.0 mm steel tip 22.7 mm long with a 1.5 mm end chamfer. It lies level, head toward +y, axis 12.1 mm over the table at (0.24, 0.26 head underside), on two black 90 deg V saddles. The barrel (25 g): 31.6 mm long, 12-sided 21.6 mm across the faces, a 9 mm bore 27 mm deep with a 2 mm mouth chamfer; it lies on a face, mouth toward +y at (0.24, -0.07). Friction (static/dynamic): bolt and barrel 0.35/0.30, hasp ears 0.30/0.25, the rest 1.2/1.0.
scoring: Through: the bolt's axis crosses the mid-plane of each of the keeper's two ears between the head and the tip end, within the hole's radial play at that point of the pin (16 mm hole minus the local pin radius) plus 0.5 mm. Seated: the barrel's axis within 6 deg of the bolt's, its mouth centre within 1.5 mm of the bolt's axis and between 1.5 mm short of and 0.5 mm past the seat on the shoulder (57.3 mm from the head). Sealed: through and seated, both ears between the head and the barrel's mouth. Clear: both grippers' gripper and finger collision hulls, read each control step, 10 mm or more from cylinders around the bolt's head, the pin and the barrel (a lower bound on the gap). Still: from the change in pose between consecutive control steps, the bolt and barrel under 5 mm/s and their axes turning under 0.05 rad/s (spin about the axis is ignored). Success (1.0): sealed at the keeper, clear, still for 1 s. Latched 0: the barrel seated while the bolt is through the handle retainer (wrong hasp) or through neither hasp (spent), or a part 30 mm below the table top (lost). Otherwise, at the last step: sealed, clear and still 0.8; sealed and clear 0.7; sealed 0.55; through the keeper with the barrel started on the tip (coaxial, short of the seat) 0.4; through the keeper 0.25; else 0.
reset_notes: Lay the bolt in its tray and the barrel on the table at their starts, apart. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate. A real barrel locks onto a groove in the tip and cannot be pulled off; here the scorer judges the seal closed once the barrel seats on the shoulder and latches a wrong or spent close, while the parts stay free in the sim. Hasp sizes are ours (real hasps vary). The seal is drawn without its printed number and the bolt has no groove. The scorer reads poses and hand hulls, not forces.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 31.95 s, step 639)
